state.task: Classify five narrow missing rules in an AI-authored CRUD business DSL. The aim is low-cost adoption through compact source, predictable authorization and transaction order. Nothing here exists as a tested runtime guarantee. Compare all candidates on their real advantages and liabilities; this exercise excludes extra data-transfer types, build files, application features, runtime code and deployment scaffolding.
state.facts: Under DESIGN section 4, read policies combine permitted fields for matching rows, while absent grants deny access and record identity, tenant and containment limits always apply. User-facing queries enforce these grants before counts or filters. Business mutations can use protected data for decisions without exposing it. The language forbids recursive pure derives yet leaves policy-internal query privilege unclear: has_role reads CompanyRole and CompanyRole read authorization calls has_role. Viewer semantics govern ordinary read=true; the already declared scope=authority explicitly permits its typed report. Sections 3 and 5–7 define version-bearing records, expected input versions, written effect order, old-state locks, final-state constraints and single-owner atomic work. Hook before/input cannot change; hook after may be edited without reentering the triggering CRUD. Scenario assignments produce change events but no CRUD hooks. Test records begin at revision 1; maintenance section 11 increments a converted row once and retains versions for pure renames. It never specifies business no-op versions or in-body visibility. The supplied examples use +1 from an ordinary alias after assignment but the hook after-side version without addition.
state.workflow: Section 6 gives recurring ticks epoch slots, missed-slot coalescing and verified trusted context with actor null. Its tenant and per-root routing remains unstated. Default stored rows belong to a team in D1; explicitly bound root records each select a SQLite Durable Object. The root discovery index is eventual and cannot authorize availability. Section 7 disallows mutation reads or writes across atomic owners and fences state, receipts, audit and outgoing intents with bounded retries. Section 5 rejects an entire provisional mutation whenever require fails; section 6 describes false trusted guards as skipped. The grammar has a single require node both outside and inside do. The included queue-handler BDD rows require rule_failed for false leading conditions; body checks in handlers also use rejection. Cancellation, supersession and false dispatch when already support skipping. Existing DeliveryResult has the five statuses pending, succeeded, failed, unknown and skipped, with safe DeliveryError code/message, so a new envelope is unnecessary.
state.files: Section 8 creates a single local R2 file store from selected source use. Completed immutable bytes pass content, MIME, byte-length and quota checks; attaching requires ownership in the active app/team/principal or read permission on an existing attachment. Neither possession of an identifier nor a web address supplies that right. The capability type system accepts eventual file results, consumed by a later local handler. The shown quotation and invoice PDF handlers attach result.document under their exact authorization and correlation conditions. A verified completion runs without a human actor; a valid result shape or successful HTTP response is not ownership evidence. The existing orphan collection horizon covers finished but unlinked uploads. Installed transport adapters own wire conversion and authentication; do not pretend a new helper exists or repair the quote handler’s missing revision comparison as part of this contract.
state.research: PostgreSQL officially documents both caller permissions for policy expressions and privileged security-definer functions, making privilege mode a substantive alternative rather than universal database behavior. SQLite documents transaction atomicity but does not decide SaaS row revisions. These external facts cannot validate an unbuilt CanLang implementation. References: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/ddl-rowsecurity.html and https://www.sqlite.org/lang_transaction.html
state.instruction: For each choice, compare the preserved facts and pick a candidate; choose unresolved when evidence cannot distinguish them. Assess the five first-listed candidates together using the binary coherence question. Retain returned probabilities without a pass cutoff, and treat the classification as advice rather than approval or an executable proof.

code.draft/CanCustomer.can:24-36:
export derive has_role(person:user,org:Customer,role:CompanyRole.role):bool = any(org.CompanyRole as grant,grant.account==person and grant.role==role and grant.active)
  export derive has_location_role(person:user,org:Customer,role:CompanyRole.role,location:Location):bool = any(org.CompanyRole as grant,grant.account==person and grant.role==role and grant.active and location in grant.locations)
  export derive owns(person:user,org:Customer):bool = org.kind==individual and any(org.Contact as contact,contact.account==person and contact.verified)
  derive customer_staff(person:user,org:Customer):bool = any(org.locations as location,can_work(person,location))
  policy Customer read=customer_reader or billing_reader where=customer_staff(actor,row) fields=name,kind,locations,active
  policy Customer read=customer_manager and customer_staff(actor,row)
  policy Customer read=authenticated where=owns(actor,row) or has_role(actor,row,administrator) or has_role(actor,row,booker) or has_role(actor,row,billing)
  policy Contact read=authenticated where=actor.email_verified and row.email==actor.email fields=name,email,account,verified
  policy Contact read=customer_reader or billing_reader where=customer_staff(actor,row.parent) fields=name,email,phone,verified
  policy Contact read=customer_manager and customer_staff(actor,row.parent)
  policy Contact read=authenticated where=row.account==actor or has_role(actor,row.parent,administrator)
  policy CompanyRole read=authenticated where=row.account==actor or has_role(actor,row.parent,administrator)
  policy CompanyRole read=customer_manager and customer_staff(actor,row.parent)
code.draft/CanStats.can:33-47:
scenario process on=WebJobs
   require event.site.active and event.occurred<=now+5m and event.occurred>now-30d
   do
    if not any(event.site.AcceptedEvent as accepted,accepted.event_id==event.event_id)
     create AcceptedEvent {parent=event.site,event_id=event.event_id,name=event.name,occurred=event.occurred,path=event.path,location=event.location,workspace=event.workspace,source=event.source,medium=event.medium,visitor=event.visitor,session=event.session,session_started=event.session_started} as accepted
     send WebDimensions.write {site=event.site.id,name=event.name,path=event.path,location=event.location,source=event.source,value=1} as telemetry
     for health in event.site.Health limit=1
      set health {accepted=health.accepted+1,last_processed=now}
   examples seed=[health] event=WebEvent {site=website,event_id="fresh",name="page_view",occurred=now,path="/"}
    website.active -> health.accepted
    true -> 1
    false -> error(rule_failed)
   examples seed=[health] event=WebEvent {site=website,event_id="expired",name="page_view",occurred=now-30d,path="/"}
    website.active -> health.accepted
    true -> error(rule_failed)
code.draft/CanBook.can:95-104:
scenario ready on=every(1m)
   do
    for appointment in Appointment as item where item.state==pending and item.host_ok and item.room_ok limit=100
     set appointment {state=confirmed}
     send Mail.send {to=appointment.contact.email,subject=format("Appointment confirmed"@{nl="Afspraak bevestigd"},locale=null),body=appointment.parent.parent.instructions} as confirmation
     if appointment.from>now+1h
      schedule appointment.id at=appointment.from-1h event=Reminder {appointment,revision=appointment.version+1}
  scenario remind on=Reminder
   require event.appointment.state==confirmed and event.appointment.version==event.revision
   do send Mail.send {to=event.appointment.contact.email,subject=format("Appointment reminder"@{nl="Afspraakherinnering"},locale=null),body=event.appointment.parent.parent.instructions} when=event.appointment.state==confirmed as notice
code.draft/CanPropose.can:66-75:
scenario document(revision:Revision) by=salesperson or authenticated label=label_QuotePdf_document
   require revision.state in [sent,accepted,declined] and ((salesperson and can_work(actor,revision.parent.location)) or (actor.email_verified and actor.email==revision.recipient_email))
   do
    send Documents.quote {source=revision.id,revision=revision.version,snapshot=QuoteDocument {issuer=revision.issuer_snapshot,recipient=revision.recipient_email,title=revision.title_snapshot,location=revision.location_snapshot,from=revision.from,until=revision.until,terms=revision.terms,expires=revision.expires,lines=revision.Item as item select QuoteLine {title=item.title,quantity=item.quantity,price=item.price,tax=item.tax,discount=item.discount},total=revision.total}} as delivery
    set revision {document_delivery=delivery.id}
  scenario document_result on=Documents.quote.completed
   do
    for revision in Revision as row where row.document_delivery==event.delivery_id limit=1
     if event.status==succeeded and event.result?.source==revision.id
      set revision {pdf=event.result.document}
code.draft/CanInvoice.can:118-126:
require invoice.state==issued and invoice.number!=null and invoice.issued_at!=null and (owns(actor,invoice.parent) or has_role(actor,invoice.parent,billing) or (finance and can_work(actor,invoice.location)))
   do
    send Documents.invoice {source=invoice.id,revision=invoice.version,snapshot=InvoiceDocument {issuer=invoice.issuer,recipient=invoice.recipient,address=invoice.address,tax_reference=invoice.tax_reference,number=invoice.number,issued_at=invoice.issued_at,due=invoice.due,currency=invoice.currency,lines=invoice.Line as line select DocumentLine {title=line.description,quantity=line.quantity,price=line.price,tax=line.tax,discount=line.discount},credits=invoice.Credit as credit select DocumentCredit {amount=credit.amount,reason=credit.reason},payments=invoice.Attempt as payment select DocumentPayment {reference=payment.reference,amount=payment.amount,state=format("{status}",{status=payment.status}),received=payment.received},total=invoice.total}} as delivery
    create DocumentRequest {parent=invoice,revision=invoice.version,delivery=delivery.id} as request
  scenario document_result on=Documents.invoice.completed
   do
    for request in DocumentRequest as row where row.delivery==event.delivery_id limit=1
     if event.status==succeeded and event.result?.source==request.parent.id and event.result.revision==request.revision
      create Document {parent=request.parent,revision=request.revision,file=event.result.document} as document

policy.instructions: Choose the privilege mode for pure expressions used to decide a read grant.

criteria.authority: Use owner-limited authoritative reads in policies, invariants, locks, CRUD eligibility and mutation/verified-handler checks, without bypassing tenant, containment or expiry. Derives follow the invoking mode; normal viewer reports remain permission-filtered and privileged reports keep scope=authority. Grant-decision scans omit recursive viewer policy filtering, while derive cycles stay invalid. Hidden grant tables then work without public disclosure, at the cost of carefully separating decision authority from return visibility.
criteria.viewer: Filter permission-predicate scans using the caller’s ordinary grants and diagnose dependency loops. Uniform query access is easier to explain and grants less internal privilege; conversely the shown self-dependent role policy needs restructuring or rejection and cannot inspect unreadable authorization rows.
criteria.unresolved: Delay the privilege rule until a concrete CompanyRole evaluation demonstrates safety, reducing premature commitment but preventing a complete current-policy target.

versions.instructions: Select row-revision visibility and advancement for ordered writes and CRUD hooks.

criteria.write_intent: A new row remains revision 1 for the whole operation. Ordinary references to old rows continue exposing input v despite seeing updated fields; targeting such a row with successful set, update or archive reserves exactly one v+1 even when values are equal. Update-hook after shows that reserved revision and before retains v; nested calls and hook edits share the increment/history event. Read-only/send-only references and unwritten parents retain v. Existing schedule expressions survive, but harmless repeated assignments still invalidate versions and add audit entries.
criteria.live_dirty: Expose v+1 consistently through ordinary references and hook after when the first normalized assignment actually differs; later assignments and restoring the original value do not advance again or undo dirtiness. Creation uses 1 and equal-value operations keep v. This saves no-op revisions and follows provisional metadata, but old post-write +1 schedules need rewrites and hook metadata depends on tracked effective edits.
criteria.unresolved: Require a small no-op/multiple-write/hook demonstration before deciding the revision rule. Deferral protects against an inconsistent choice but prevents reliable current reminder and library contracts.

ticks.instructions: Pick the routing rule for every invocations with no authored record parameter.

criteria.per_scope: Derive one compatible routing kind from the handler’s owner-scoped queries and writes: active-team instances for D1 team data, a single app occurrence for app-only state, or each authoritative Durable Object root. Restrict evaluation to that instance and reject mixed incompatible owners. Identity combines release/handler, scope and epoch slot; recover missed slots separately per scope, and begin newly created scopes at the next slot. This keeps tenant recurrence concise, while full authoritative instance discovery is an unbuilt coverage obligation.
criteria.d1_first: Specify team/app D1 fanout only and issue a diagnostic for per-root every or incompatible scopes. Per-record schedule remains available instead. Less automatic root enumeration needs proving, but per-root recurrence must be armed explicitly and every remains restricted.
criteria.unresolved: Postpone recurring routing until isolation and instance-coverage evidence exists. Avoid assuming tenant selection, but acknowledge that the demonstrated recurring handlers still lack execution semantics.

requires.instructions: Choose production and BDD behavior when a trusted require is false.

criteria.business_error: Treat all authored checks identically: return a safe business rejection, normally rule_failed, discard every proposed write/intent, and finish the trusted occurrence as failed rather than retrying it. Lifecycle cancellation/supersession/expiry/invalidation and false dispatch when remain skips. Tests assert this same invocation error. Existing Stats rows remain meaningful; stale scheduled checks create failed operational records instead of skip records.
criteria.leading_skip: Use skipped for a false pre-do trusted guard but business rejection for a false body check, with full rollback in either case. Test expected skipped through the actual terminal outcome, correcting the two Stats error expectations. Stale occurrences gain quieter disposition, but guard placement now determines outcome and the draft examples change.
criteria.unresolved: Expose the contradiction until a terminal-result policy is chosen, without relabeling skips as errors; this keeps semantics honest but leaves handler tests unresolved.

files.instructions: Choose an authorization/finalization boundary for typed remote PDF results.

criteria.receiver_finalize: Import and validate the immutable content using the recipient’s canonical upload flow before emitting succeeded. Runtime-only provenance associates recipient app/team/owner, originating person or trusted ingress, bound adapter, delivery identity and field location. The associated completion may attach under that provenance without a human actor substitution. Replays reuse the delivery/field object and reject changed bytes; uncommitted local attachments leave an orphan for normal cleanup. No R2/owner transaction is promised. Existing types remain usable, but byte transfer and local quota/finalization obligations grow.
criteria.provider_reference: Keep an immutable provider object and verify explicit delegated attachment/download rights and its retention period. Reduced local copying is possible, but a cross-owner file-access/lifetime contract must supplement current local-store rules; possession of a link or identifier is never sufficient.
criteria.reject_remote_file: Disallow remote outputs containing file while handoff is unavailable. Attachment privilege remains defensible, at the expense of refusing the present quotation/invoice document interfaces until they are redesigned.
criteria.unresolved: Preserve a declared but unfinished remote-file boundary instead of fabricating permission. The app examples remain inspectable but their PDF attachment path cannot run.

coherence.instructions: Is the five-part authority/write-intent/per-scope/business-error/receiver-finalization proposal internally compatible with the shown ordered effects, local ownership, read grants and production-path examples?

criteria.true: No demonstrated contract conflict remains in the proposal and its implementation obligations are explicit, so it is suitable as draft wording rather than a runtime claim.
criteria.false: A concrete clash in the proposal means it needs revision before integration despite any benefits of separate parts.
